key_insight: Among patients who survived hospitalization for stroke, cardiac disease led subsequent deaths after ischemic stroke, while cancer led after hemorrhagic stroke.
clinical_relevance: These findings support research into subtype-specific follow-up, including longitudinal cardiac and sudden-death risk assessment after ischemic stroke.
method: Identified 1,344 adults hospitalized with stroke in the Cedars-Sinai OSCAR cohort during 2017–2020.
Used billing codes, imaging, and large language model-assisted chart review; classified causes of death into 10 categories.
Followed patients through June 30, 2025, comparing mortality patterns by stroke subtype and hospitalization survival.
evidence_signal: Among 1,141 discharged survivors, 625 died over a median 5.2-year follow-up; cardiac disease accounted for 31.6% of deaths after ischemic stroke and cancer for 38.9% after hemorrhagic stroke.
watch_item: This observational, single-health-system study identifies mortality patterns but does not establish whether subtype-specific surveillance improves outcomes.
paper_title: Divergent Causes of Death After Ischemic and Hemorrhagic Stroke in the Reperfusion Era: A Contemporary Cohort Study
